chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who made a bequest, while his heirs were witnesses, and they approved that. Then when the man died, they revoked the bequest. Do they have the right to reject what they had acknowledged?
So he عليه السلام said: “They do not have that right, and the bequest is binding upon them when they had acknowledged it during his lifetime.”

key_terms.شُهُودٌ: Witnesses; here indicating that the heirs were present and aware
key_terms.نَقَضُوا الْوَصِيَّةَ: They revoked or tried to undo the bequest
key_terms.وَرَثَتُهُ: His heirs, those entitled to inherit from him
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: A bequest or will made by a person concerning his estate

ai.seo_question: Can heirs revoke a will after the deceased has died if they had already approved it during his lifetime?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a bequest that heirs approved while the testator was still alive. Once they acknowledged it during his lifetime, they cannot revoke it after his death, and the bequest remains binding upon them.
